G3802:
παγιδεύω
(παγίς), [in LXX: 1Ki.28:9 (נָקַשׁ hith.), Ecc.9:12 (יָקֹשׁ pu.)* ;]
to ensnare: metaphorically, with accusative, ἐν λόγῳ, Mat.22:15 (not elsewhere).†

G3803:
παγίς, -ίδος, ή
(πήγνυμι), [in LXX for פַּח, מוֹקֵשׁ, רֶשֶׁת, etc. ;]
poët. (Aristoph., al.) and late for πάγη, a trap, snare; metaphorically (as also in cl.): Luk.21:35, Rom.11:9" (LXX) 1Ti.3:7 6:9, 2Ti.2:26.†
(AS)
G3804:
πάθημα, -τος, τό
(πάσχω), like πάθος,
1. that which befalls one, a suffering, affliction: pl., Rom.8:18, 2Co.1:6-7, Col.1:24, 2Ti.3:11, Heb.2:10 10:32, 1Pe.5:9; of Christ's sufferings: τὰ εἰς Χ., 1Pe.1:11; τ. Χριστσῦ, 1Pe.5:1; id. as shared by Christians, 2Co.1:5, Php.3:10, 1Pe.4:13.

SYN.: see: πάθος (AS)
G3805:
παθητός, -ή, -όν
(πάσχω),
1. one who has suffered.
2. subject to suffering (R, mg., see M, Pr., 222) or destined to suffer (AV, R, txt.): Act.26:23.†
(AS)
G3806:
πάθος, -ους, τό
(πάιτχω), [in LXX: Job.30:31 (אֵבֶל), Pro.25:20, and very frequently in (4Ma.1:1 n, al.)* ;]
like πάθημα;
1. that which befalls one, that which one suffers
2. a passive emotion or affection (esp. of violent emotion), a passion, passionate desire; in NT always in bad sense: Col.3:5; π. ἀτιμίας, Rom.1:26; π. ἐπιθυμίας, 1Th.4:5.†
SYN.: π. = πάθημα, exc. that πάθημα is the more concrete and particular. In NT usage, π. represents the passive, ungoverned aspect of evil desire, as opposite to ἐπιθυμία, which is the active and also the more comprehensive term (see Tr., Syn., LXXxvii); cf. also ὄρεξις (AS)
G3807:
παιδαγωγός, -oῦ, ὁ
(παῖς, ἄγω),
a guide, guardian, trainer of boys, a tutor (disting. from διδάσκαλος, Xen., Lac., 3, 1), usually a trusty slave: opposite to πατήρ, 1Co.4:15; figuratively, of the Law, π. εἰς Χριστόν, Gal.3:24-25.†

G3808:
παιδάριον, -ου, τό dimin. of παῖς,

G3809:
παιδεία (-ία, Τ), -ας, ἡ
(παιδεύω), [in LXX chiefly for מוּסָר ;]
1. the rearing of a child (Æsch.).

(AS)
G3810:

1. prop., a teacher, instructor: Rom.2:20.

(AS)
G3811:
παιδεύω
(παίς), [in LXX chiefly for יָסַר ;]
1. as in cl., to train children, hence, generally, to teach, instruct: Act.7:22 22:3, 1Ti.1:20, Tit.2:12.

G3812:
παιδιόθεν
(παιδίον),
adv., [in LXX: Gen.47:3 * ;]
= cl. ἐκ παιδός, παιδίον, from childhood: Mrk.9:21.†

G3813:
παιδίον, -ου, τό dimin, of παῖς,

G3815:
παίζω

G3816:

G3817:
παίω
[in LXX chiefly for נָכָה hi. ;]
to strike, smite: with the hand or fist, Mat.26:68, Luk.22:64; with a sword, Mrk.14:47, Jhn.18:10; of a reptile, to sting: Rev.9:5.†
(AS)
G3819:
πάλαι
adv. of time, [in LXX: Isa.48:5, 7 (אָז), etc. ;]
long ago, of old, in time past (denoting past time absolutely, as πρότερον relatively) : Mat.11:21, Luk.10:13, Heb.1:1, Ju 4; as adj., with art., 2Pe.1:9; of time just past, Mrk.6:47 (WH, mg.), Mrk.15:44 (WH, mg., R, txt.); with durst. praes. (RV, all this time), 2Co.12:19.†
(AS)
G3820:
παλαιός, -ά, -όν
(πάλαι), [in LXX: Lev.25:22 26:10, Sng.7:13 (14) (יָשֵׁן), יָשֵׁן), Jos.9:4-5, Jer.38:11 (בָּלֶה), etc. ;]

G3822:

πάλη, -ης, ἡ

G3826:
πανπληθεί (Rec. παμπλ-, see WH, App., 150),

G3831:
πανήγυρις, -εως, ἡ

G3832:

G3834:
πανουργία, -ας, ἡ

G3837:
πανταχοῦ
adv., [in LXX: Isa.42:22 (כָּלַם)* ;]
everywhere: Mrk.1:28 16:20, Luk.9:6, Act.17:30 24:3 28:22, 1Co.4:17.†

G3838:
παντελής, -ές
(πᾶς, τέλος), [in LXX: 3Ma.7:16 A* ;]
all-complete, entire, perfect; εἰς τ. παντελές, completely, utterly: Luk.13:11, Heb.7:25 (where perhaps in temp. sense, finally; see MM, xviii).†

G3839:
πάντῃ (Rec. -τη),

G3840:
πάντοθεν

G3845:
παρα-βαίνω
[in LXX for סוּר, עָבַר, פָּרַר, שָׂטָה, etc. ;]
1. in Hom. (twice), to go by the side of, stand beside.
2. (AS)
G3846:
παρα-βάλλω
[in LXX: Pro.2:2 4:20 5:1, 13 22:17 (נָטָה hi.), Rut.2:16 (שָׁלַל), 2Ma.14:38 (elsewhere as seel.4)* ;]

2. to lay beside, compare (Hdt., Plat., al.): Mrk.4:30, Rec.
3. Reflexive, to betake oneself, come near; of seamen, to cross over: εἰς Σάμον, Act.20:15.
4. In mid. = παραβολεύομαι, which see†

G3847:
παρά-βασις, -εως, ἡ
(παραβαίνω), [in LXX: Psa.101:3 (שֵׂט), 4Ki.2:24 A, Wis.14:31, 2Ma.15:10 * ;]
1. a going aside, a deviation (Arist.).
2. In later writers, an overstepping; metaphorically, transgression (Plut., al.) : Rom.4:15 5:14, Heb.2:2 9:15; τ. νόμου, Rom.2:23; ἐν π., 1Ti.2:14; τ. παραβάσεων χάριν, Gal.3:19
SYN.: see: ἁμαρτία (AS)
G3848:
παρα-βάτης, -ου, ὁ
(παραβαίνω), [in Sm.: Psa.17:4 139:19, Jer.6:28 * ;]
1. one who stands beside, the warrior who stands by the charioteer (of. παραβαίνω, 1).
2. a transgressor (Æsch., παρβάτης): Gal.2:18, Jas.2:9; π. νόμου, Rom.2:25, 27, Jas.2:11.†
(AS)
G3849:
παρα-βιάζομαι
[in LXX: Gen.19:9, 4Ki.2:17 (פָּצַר), Deu.1:43 (זוּד hi.), 1Ki.28:23 (פָּרַץ) see1. 4 * ;]

2. to compel by force (Polyb.).
3. to constrain by entreaty (Ge, 1Sam, ll. with): Luk.24:29, Act.16:15.†
(AS)
G3850:
παραβολή, -ῆς, ἡ
(παραβάλλω), [in LXX (cf. McNeile, Mt., 185): Num.23:7, Deu.28:37, Psa.44:14, Pro.1:6, Eze.12:22, al. (מָשַׁל), Sir.47:17 (חִידָה), al. mutt. in Sir, Wis.5:3 ;]

4 4 Like Heb. מָשַׁל (1Ki.10:12, Pro.1:6, Sir.3:29, al.), = παροιμία, a proverb or gnomic saying: Luk.4:23 5:36 6:39

G3851:
παρα-βολεύομαι

παρα-βουλεύομαι,

G3852:
παρ-αγγελία, -ας, ἡ

(AS)

SYN.: see: ἐντέλλω (AS)
G3854:
παρα-γίνομαι
